sampling_model.design: No statistical sampling; the input is one explicitly encoded finite acyclic NSCM and one designated actual solution.
sampling_model.units: Vertices, domain values, local-table rows, output incidences, graph edges, and rational cost records counted by \(L\).
sampling_model.treatment: The singleton counterfactual intervention changes \(X=a_X\) to some \(X=x'\ne a_X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; local tables are total and all finite domains are explicitly enumerated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the local relations are supplied exactly rather than estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, proved on page 532, gives a same-signature representative that is both a structural simplification of the original model and a witness to the actual-cause counterfactual dependence.
Acyclic nondeterministic SCMs use set-valued mechanisms and preserve the designated actual solution under counterfactual evaluation.
Bounded-domain, bounded-width causal trees and layered graphs permit polynomial Halpern--Pearl cause decisions.
Halpern--Pearl weak and actual cause problems have definition-dependent hardness classifications.
The updated Halpern--Pearl definition changes the exact complexity of computing actual causes.
Binary acyclic Halpern--Pearl actual-cause checking can be encoded as satisfiability.
Binary Halpern--Pearl checking and inference can be formulated as ILP and MaxSAT optimization.
Adjustable beam search approximately identifies Halpern--Pearl-style causes in non-Boolean and stochastic systems.

body.tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but the definition has no exact algorithmic frontier. Under the backend-motivated computational restrictions of finite explicit local tables and a full graph on \(U\cup V\) whose undirected skeleton is a forest, the project derives a cost-preserving compiler and a complete value-path certificate. A linear-arithmetic dynamic program returns a witness and optimum certificate or a separating cut, while a selector-and-clause construction proves NP-completeness even when every variable is binary and deterministic and the endogenous graph is one directed chain. A parameterized shared-selector family pinpoints why the endogenous value-set state used in classical Halpern--Pearl causal-tree propagation cannot by itself audit Beckers deletion legality, without modifying the published Halpern--Pearl theorem.

project_justification.gap: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual supplies a same-signature structural-simplification representative but no compiler, certificate system, minimum-cost result, or complexity classification. Existing causal-tree algorithms and SAT encodings concern Halpern--Pearl causation and do not enforce Beckers's full-graph reachability legality or actual-row freezing.
project_justification.niche: The novel computational scope restricts attention to finite explicitly encoded tables and, for the positive result, a forest skeleton on the full vertex set \(U\cup V\). These backend-motivated restrictions make row-level support auditing and unique-path composition possible without attributing them to Beckers or Eiter--Lukasiewicz.
project_justification.fill: The project proves an extensional compiler theorem, an exact additive optimum formula with independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates, and a restricted NP-completeness theorem. The parameterized shared-selector obstruction shows precisely why two deletion histories with the same endogenous value state can differ in full-graph legality.

body.related_work: Beckers2025Actual, Section 5.1, Definitions 13, 15, and 16 on pages 523--524 and Section 6, Definitions 18 and 19 and Proposition 20 on page 525, supplies the structural-simplification and actual-causation semantics that the compiler must implement; the proof of Proposition 20 appears on page 532. It is semantic prior art and contains no algorithmic frontier. Beckers2025NCM supplies set-valued equations and topological counterfactual semantics, but the finite explicit encoding imposed here is a novel computational-scope restriction rather than a standard Beckers assumption. The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, is the closest methodological comparator: its Halpern--Pearl causal-tree analysis recursively stores families of subsets of each endogenous path-variable domain. Its published theorem is left intact; the proposition for \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) shows only that a direct transfer of that unaugmented \(G[V]\)-only state type to Beckers deletion legality loses shared-exogenous reachability information. Requiring the full graph on \(U\cup V\) to be a polyforest is therefore a novel backend scope condition, not the causal-tree condition of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable. EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 show that complexity is definition-sensitive, but neither result concerns Beckers's deletion operation or full exogenous graph. IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT proves a Boolean SAT translation for Halpern--Pearl checking, while IbrahimPretschner2020Optimization attaches optimization objectives to binary Halpern--Pearl constraints. ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search motivates software-facing non-Boolean and stochastic search, but its adjustable beam search targets Halpern--Pearl-style causes and does not give exact negative or optimum certificates. These sources inform the semantics, propagation, reduction, and compiler architecture; no theorem-level extension of their estimands or encodings is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The full-unicycle question is intentionally unresolved. No claim is made for general full-graph treewidth, succinct mechanisms, continuous domains, negative deletion costs, unrestricted polynomial negative certificates, or unrestricted parsimonious counting. The selector reduction gives a bijection only after normalizing certificates; unrestricted successful graphs can encode one satisfying assignment in several ways and normalization need not preserve cost.
body.honest_scope: The local hitting lemma, forest completion, optimum recurrence, rational arithmetic bound, shared-selector obstruction, and selector implications are theorem obligations despite strong finite presolve evidence. The central unresolved verification task is the end-to-end arbitrary-domain compiler and independent verifier, including the order of actual-row freezing, preservation of the retained graph and charged deletions, and topological completion. Finiteness, explicit table encoding, and requiring the full graph on \(U\cup V\) to be a polyforest are novel computational-scope restrictions motivated by the backend rather than assumptions inherited from Beckers or Eiter--Lukasiewicz. As a sanity reduction, when all tables are deterministic and the full graph is a directed tree, the certificate becomes unique-path value propagation of the same structural form as the known causal-tree recurrence, while retaining Beckers rather than Halpern--Pearl local semantics.
